context_needed: Cross-sectional survey of 1,538 poor, mainly ethnic-minority households in Ha Giang province, Vietnam (abstract, p. 1; study area p. 10). The human-support sample has 1,197 households: 410 received governmental human-capacity support and 787 received no support (p. 20). Estimand: ATET. MPI is a multidimensional poverty index from 0 to 1 (lower is better), and 'multidimensionally poor' is a 0/1 indicator for MPI at or above 1/3 (p. 20). The authors' main estimator is IPWRA (Table 6, p. 20: -0.039 (0.008) on MPI and -0.093 (0.042) on being poor). Tables 14 and 15 report the robustness estimators listed on p. 17, so none of these columns is the preferred one. Column (4) is a fractional probit for the MPI share and a plain probit for the 0/1 outcome: it is an outcome model, not a participation model.

rule: When one effect is estimated by several matching or weighting estimators side by side, store one row per estimator and put the estimator (and its covariate set) in 'specification'. Potential-outcome means, covariate Yes/No rows, outcome means and sensitivity breakdowns are never effects. Mark 'preferred' only on the estimator the authors call main, which here sits in another table (IPWRA, Table 6).
